entries.source: Urkundenbuch des Cistercienserstiftes B. Mariae V. zu Hohenfurt in Böhmen, Nr. CCXLIV. , S. 317, CCXLIV.
entries.german:
1464. 1. August. 0. �?0. — Abt Thomas von Hohenfurt und der Convent daselbst urkunden über die vor 39 Jahren von Ulrich von Rosenberg dem Herrn von Walsee in Österreich verpfändeten und nun durch Johann von Rosenberg, den Sohn Ulrichs, wieder ausgelösten Kleinodien ihres Stiftet.

CCXLIV. Sohn Ulrichs, wieder ausgelösten Kleinodien ihres Stiftet. Nos frater Thomas abbas totusque conuentus monasterii Alto- uadensis ad futuram rei memoriam per presentes litteras deducimus successoribus et fratribus nostris, quomodo olim et generosus domi- nus dominus Vlricus de Rozmberg temporibus periculosis et gwera- rum pro defensione fidei christiane et tuicione dominii sui, sub qua monastcrium nostrum tamquam veri patroni consistit, acceptis cleno- diis cum reliquiis infrascriptis a menasterio ea cum aliis clenodiis generoso domino de Wolse residente in Austria pignorauit, vbi per quadraginta annos minus vno sic extra terram Bohemio et monaste- rium nostrum aliónala fuerunt, et nobilis et generosus dominus Jobannes predicti domini Ylrici lilins subscripta clenodia cum aliis suis clenodiis exsoluit; volentes ut honor omnipotentis dei beate vir- ginis Marie et omnium sanctorum non minuatur per alienacionem vlteriorem, sed pocius augeatur per exsolucionem, clenodia infra scripta cum magnis laboribus et impensis partem eciam bonorum in- niobilium monasterii nostri propter hoc obligantes a predicto domino nostro gracioso exsoluimus et liberauimus: tabulam argenteam et deauratam cum crinibus sanete Marie Magdalene et monstranciam cum dente sancti Benedicti, tabulam cum rosis, que ob remedium anime nobilis domine Katherine de Sawnberg matre nobilium domino- rum Petri Jodoci Vlrici et Johannis monasterio nostro donata sunt cum calice aureo infrascripto. Item magnam crucem auream, quam legauit dominus Zawissius. Item calicem cum rosis, quem cum volun tate domini Johannis tune monasterio ad Budwais vendidimus. Item tres calices, quos ab eo de nouo emimus, pro quibus omnibus dedi- mus sexingentos florenos Vngaricales. Item in speciali pro parua cruce aurea, quam donauit nobilis dominus Henricus primus pater domini Petri de Rozmberg, et pro vno calice aureo, de quo supra mentid facta est, ducentas sexagenas grossorum exsoluimus. Et ultra predictas summas super addidimus steuram a nostris subditis per- ceptam centum viginti quinque sexagenas grossorum. Et debitum 304 nostrum triginta duarum sexagenarum, quod et in parata pecunia per prius eomodauerimus, remisimus tali condicione pacto fide et iura mento ac pena sponte appositis per predictum dominum Johannem, quod predictus domains dominus Johannes promisit honorifice fideliter et vere pro se et pro suis heredibus et successoribus omni potenti deo et eius venerabili matri Marie et omnibus sanctis supra- dicta clenodia et reliquias nunquam perpetue ab eodem monasterio nostro alienare uel recipere aliquo modo, obligans se ipsum heredes ac successores suos, quod si contra illa, que suprascripta sunt, attemptaret uel attemptarent et ea non obseruant, quod ipse et illi scire debet et debent, se indignacionem omnipotentis dei gloriose Virginia Marie et omnium sanctorum incurrisse pro huiusmodi alie- naeione uel recepcione in die judicii districtissimam racionem red- diturum vel reddituros, iuxta quod lacius in littera domini Johann is desuper confecta ac maiori sigillo suo roborata ¡sta omnia continen- tur. In quorum eciam omnium predictorum futuram memoriam sigil- lum nostrum abbatis et conuentus presentibus sunt appensa. Et petiuimus reuerendum in Christo patrem dominum dominum Wilhel- mum abbatem et visitatorem nostrum de Hylaria et venerabiles decretorum doctores Nicolaum de Crumpnaw archidiaconum Bechi- nensem et Johannem de Crumpnaw archidiaconum Pragensem, qui- bus ista constabant, quod sigilla sua ad hanc lilteram nostram appen- derunt. Datum anno domini millesimo quadringentesimo sexagesimo quarto prima die mensis Augusti. Die Siegel fehlen.
entries.english:
1464 August 1. Hohenfurt. — Thomas, Abt zu Hohenfurt and the convent there issue a document concerning the monastery’s jewels, pledged 39 years earlier by Ulrich von Rosenberg to Lord von Walsee in Austria and now redeemed by Johann von Rosenberg, Ulrich’s son.

CCXLIV. Ulrich’s son redeems the monastery’s jewels. We, Brother Thomas, Abt, and the entire convent of the monastery of Hohenfurt, bring to the knowledge of our successors and brethren for the future record, by these present letters, how once, in perilous times and during wars, the noble lord Ulrich von Rosenberg, for the defense of the Christian faith and the protection of his lordship, under which our monastery stands as its true patron, took the jewels with the relics listed below from the monastery and pledged them, together with other jewels, to the noble lord von Walsee, residing in Austria. Thus they remained outside the land of Bohemia and alienated from our monastery for nearly forty years. The noble and generous lord Johann, son of the aforesaid lord Ulrich, redeemed the jewels listed below together with other jewels of his own. Wishing that the honor of Almighty God, the Blessed Virgin Mary, and all the saints should not be diminished by further alienation but rather increased by their redemption, we redeemed and freed the jewels written below from our gracious lord, with great labor and expense, also pledging part of our monastery’s real property for this purpose: a silver-gilt panel containing hairs of Saint Mary Magdalene, and a monstrance containing a tooth of Saint Benedict; a panel with roses, which was given to our monastery, together with the gold chalice listed below, for the salvation of the soul of the noble lady Katherine von Saunberg, mother of the noble lords Peter, Jodocus, Ulrich, and Johann; also a large gold cross bequeathed by Lord Zawissius; a chalice with roses, which, with the consent of Lord Johann, we then sold to the monastery at Budweis; and three chalices newly bought from him. For all these we paid 600 Hungarian gulden. In particular, for the small gold cross donated by the noble lord Heinrich the First, father of Lord Peter von Rosenberg, and for one gold chalice mentioned above, we paid 200 score groschen. In addition to these sums we added 125 score groschen from the tax collected from our subjects. We remitted our debt of 32 score groschen, which we had previously borrowed in cash, on the following condition, agreement, pledge, and penalty, voluntarily stipulated by the aforesaid Lord Johann: the aforesaid Lord Johann promised honorably, faithfully, and truly, for himself and his heirs and successors, to Almighty God, His venerable mother Mary, and all the saints, that he would never again alienate the aforesaid jewels and relics from our monastery, or take them in any way, forever; he bound himself, his heirs, and successors that, should he or they attempt or fail to observe what is written above, he and they shall know that they have incurred the displeasure of Almighty God, the glorious Virgin Mary, and all the saints, and shall render the strictest account on Judgment Day for such alienation or taking, as is set out more fully in the letter of Lord Johann made concerning this matter and confirmed with his great seal, which contains all these particulars. For the future remembrance of all the aforesaid matters, we have also attached the seal of our abbot and convent to this document. We also requested the Reverend Father in Christ, Lord Wilhelm, abbot and our visitor of Hilaria, and the venerable doctors of canon law Nicolaus of Crumpnaw, archdeacon of Bechin, and Johann of Crumpnaw, archdeacon of Prague, who knew these matters, to attach their seals to this letter. Given in the year of the Lord 1464, on the first day of August. The seals are missing.
